written: 2026-11-10, before any credal band was computed
question: Is the belief-based channel preference an artifact of one prior, or does it hold across every prior compatible with the evidence?

families.tv_ball (PRIMARY): per-component prior Beta(2m, 2(1-m)) with m in a [0.5-TV, 0.5+TV] ball (9-point grid, endpoints and 0.5 included, clipped to [0.05, 0.95]), independent across (W, Theta0, Theta1); TV = max reference-to-evaluation total-variation distance over sources from the ch.7 audit
families.stress_fixed_strength: per-component prior Beta(c, c), c in {0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4} (a 16x strength range; fixed, not data-derived)
families.extra_evidence_discount: counts tempered per component by lambda in [1-TV, 1] (5-point grid), base prior Beta(1,1); beyond the proposal, answers the 'robust only by sample size' objection

verdict_rule: robust iff the [min,max] bands of the two channel one-step values are disjoint under the PRIMARY family; winner = point-argmax channel; confirmed iff the frozen protocol's per-state advantage (ESE of other action minus ESE of preferred action) is > 0. Prior families use only the ch.7 TV distances and fixed constants; never tuned on held-out error.
rationale: Point value ratios are 45x-470x in all four states; every family perturbs O(1) prior pseudo-counts against n=8..512 observations, so values move by O(1) factors and disjointness should survive. FMoW's primary band is nearly a point (TV 0.0145 is tiny), so its robustness is only meaningfully stressed by the 16x family. If P1-P4 hold, the FMoW held-out failure is NOT prior sensitivity: the preference is robust across priors yet empirically wrong, so the Beta source-mixture channel model itself is misspecified on FMoW -- the stronger finding. CAMELYON17 would then be a robust-and-confirmed success at ~25x larger measured TV, dissociating measured law shift from where the belief-based preference fails.
falsified_if: any selected state is fragile under the primary family, or any quantitative P1-P6 item fails
exploratory_no_verdict: candidate-state fragility rates (does the band ever say fragile: test teeth)
break-even prior strength k* (how much prior weight would flip a preference)
